5102-the-path-of-a-star.title: The Path Of A Star
5102-the-path-of-a-star.creator: Mrs. Everard Cotes
5102-the-path-of-a-star.description: A book by Mrs. Everard Cotes. Her gaze embraced Miss Filbert as a person, and Miss Filbert as a pictorial fact, but that was because she could not help it. Her eyes were really engaged only with the latter Miss Filbert.

arxiv-1802-08453.title: Non-Relativistic Maxwell Chern-Simons Gravity Preprint: CECS-PHY-17/05, ICCUB-18-001
arxiv-1802-08453.creator: Luis Avilés, Ernesto Frodden, Joaquim Gomis, Diego Hidalgo, Jorge Zanelli
arxiv-1802-08453.description: Abstract We consider a non-relativistic ( NR ) limit of ( 2 + 1 ) (2+1) -dimensional Maxwell Chern-Simons ( CS ) gravity with gauge algebra [Maxwell] ⊕ u ⁡ ( 1 ) ⊕ u ⁡ ( 1 ) \oplus\ u(1)\oplus u(1) . We obtain a finite NR CS gravity with a degenerate invariant bilinear form.

arxiv-1905-08051.title: Distributed Algorithms for Subgraph-Centric Graph Platforms
arxiv-1905-08051.creator: Diptanshu Kakwani 1,∗ and Yogesh Simmhan 2
arxiv-1905-08051.description: Abstract Graph analytics for large scale graphs has gained interest in recent years. Many graph algorithms have been designed for vertex-centric distributed graph processing frameworks to operate on large graphs with 100 ​ M 100~M vertices and edges, using commodity clusters and Clouds. Subgraph-centric programming models have shown additional performance benefits than vertex-centric models.

arxiv-2104-03515.title: Reconstructing Recognizable 3D Face Shapes based on 3D Morphable Models
arxiv-2104-03515.creator: D. W. Fellner 1,2 and S. Behnke 2 1 TU Darmstadt & Fraunhofer IGD, Germany 2 Graz University of Technology, Institute of Computer Graphics and Knowledge Visualization, Austria, Diqiong Jiang 1 , Yiwei Jin 1 , Fang-Lue Zhang 2 , Yu-Kun Lai 3 , Risheng Deng 1 , Ruofeng Tong 1 , and Min Tang 1 1 Zhejia
arxiv-2104-03515.description: Abstract Many recent works have reconstructed distinctive 3D face shapes by aggregating shape parameters of the same identity and separating those of different people based on parametric models (e.g., 3D morphable models (3DMMs)). However, despite the high accuracy in the face recognition task using these shape parameters, the visual discrimination of face shapes reconstructed from those parameters remains unsatisfactory.

arxiv-2111-03621.title: A ‘Rosetta stone’ for the population dynamics of spiking neuron networks
arxiv-2111-03621.creator: Gianni V. Vinci, Maurizio Mattia
arxiv-2111-03621.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Gianni V. Vinci, Maurizio Mattia. Populations of spiking neuron models have densities of their microscopic variables (e.g., single-cell membrane potentials) whose evolution fully capture the collective dynamics of biological networks, even outside equilibrium. Despite its general applicability, the Fokker-Planck equation governing such evolution is mainly studied within the borders of the linear response theory, although alternative spectral expansion approaches offer some advantages in the study of the out-of-equilibrium dynamics.

arxiv-2202-03639.title: Contrastive predictive coding for Anomaly Detection in Multi-variate Time Series Data
arxiv-2202-03639.creator: Theivendiram Pranavan, Terence SimSchool of Computing, NUSSingaporeArulmurugan Ambikapathi, Savitha Ramasamy, Institute for Infocomm Research, (IR), A*STARSingapore
arxiv-2202-03639.description: Abstract Anomaly detection in multi-variate time series (MVTS) data is a huge challenge as it requires simultaneous representation of long term temporal dependencies and correlations across multiple variables. More often, this is solved by breaking the complexity through modeling one dependency at a time.

arxiv-2211-08289.title: More axions from diluted domain walls
arxiv-2211-08289.creator: Keisuke Harigaya, Lian-Tao Wang
arxiv-2211-08289.description: Abstract We consider the scenario in which the Peccei-Quinn symmetry breaking is followed by a period of inflation. A particularly interesting case is that the string-domain wall network produced by the symmetry breaking enters the horizon after the QCD phase transition.

arxiv-2304-04787.title: Proof of a Stable Fixed Point for Strongly Correlated Electron Matter
arxiv-2304-04787.creator: Jinchao Zhao 1 , Gabriele La Nave 2 , and Philip W. Phillips 1
arxiv-2304-04787.description: Abstract We establish the Hatsugai-Kohmoto model as a stable quartic fixed point (distinct from Wilson-Fisher) by computing the β − \beta- function in the presence of perturbing local interactions. In vicinity of the half-filled doped Mott state, the β − \beta- function vanishes for all local interactions regardless of their sign.

arxiv-2306-04756.title: A Linearly Convergent GAN Inversion-based Algorithm for Reverse Engineering of Deceptions
arxiv-2306-04756.creator: Darshan Thaker, Paris Giampouras, René Vidal
arxiv-2306-04756.description: Abstract An important aspect of developing reliable deep learning systems is devising strategies that make these systems robust to adversarial attacks. There is a long line of work that focuses on developing defenses against these attacks, but recently, researchers have began to study ways to reverse engineer the attack process .

arxiv-2403-07423.title: On the locomotion of the slider within a self-adaptive beam-slider system Journal: NLM
arxiv-2403-07423.creator: Florian Müller 1 , Malte Krack 2
arxiv-2403-07423.description: Abstract A beam-slider system is considered whose passive self-adaption relies on an intricate locomotion process involving both frictional and unilateral contact. The system also exploits geometric nonlinearity to achieve broadband efficacy. The dynamics of the system take place on three distinct time scales: On the fast time scale of the harmonic base excitation are the vibrations and the locomotion cycle.

arxiv-2407-04325.title: Understanding the Role of Invariance in Transfer Learning
arxiv-2407-04325.creator: Till Speicher tspeicher@mpi-sws.org, Vedant Nanda vnanda@mpi-sws.org, Krishna P. Gummadi gummadi@mpi-sws.org
arxiv-2407-04325.description: Abstract Transfer learning is a powerful technique for knowledge-sharing between different tasks. Recent work has found that the representations of models with certain invariances, such as to adversarial input perturbations, achieve higher performance on downstream tasks. These findings suggest that invariance may be an important property in the context of transfer learning.

pmc-10709575.title: A realistic computational model for the formation of a Place Cell
pmc-10709575.creator: Camille Mazzara, Michele Migliore
pmc-10709575.description: Hippocampal Place Cells (PCs) are pyramidal neurons showing spatially localized firing when an animal gets into a specific area within an environment. Because of their obvious and clear relation with specific cognitive functions, Place Cells operations and modulations are intensely studied experimentally.

pmc-11547509.title: Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization Analysis of Genetic Proxies of Plasma Fatty Acids and Pre-Eclampsia Risk
pmc-11547509.creator: Jingqi Zhou, Shuo Jiang, Dangyun Liu, Xinyi Li, Ziyi Zhou, Zhiheng Wang, Hui Wang
pmc-11547509.description: Background: Previous studies have reported associations between fatty acids and the risk of pre-eclampsia. However, the causality of these associations remains uncertain. This study postulates a causal relationship between specific plasma fatty acids and pre-eclampsia or other maternal hypertensive disorders (PE-HTPs). To test this hypothesis, two-sample bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses were employed to determine the causality effects.

pmc-11603504.title: Occurrence of patellofemoral osteoarthritis at medium and long terms in patients undergoing isolated reconstruction of the medial patellofemoral ligment with the medial third of the patellar tendon
pmc-11603504.creator: F Kupczik, RG Gobbi, MEG Schiavon, B Sbrissia, MD Brunet, GL Camanho
pmc-11603504.description: ObjectivesThe purpose of this study was to analyze the presence of patellofemoral osteoarthritis (OA) in the medium and long term in patients undergoing reconstruction of the medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) with a medial strip of the patellar tendon to treat recurrent patellar instability.

pmc-11658531.title: Pediatric to adult primary care transition for medically complex youth: A tale of learning from challenges experienced implementing a pilot project during COVID-19
pmc-11658531.creator: Reem Hasan, Reyna Lindert, Danielle Sullivan, Shreya Roy, Alison J. Martin
pmc-11658531.description: PurposeThe aim of our article is to describe our learning based on challenges encountered implementing two related pediatric to adult primary care transition pilots for medically complex adolescents and young adults as part of the Children with Medical Complexity Collaborative for Improvement and Innovation Network.DesignWe undertook two sequential pilot projects.

pmc-11733621.title: EPA guidance on lifestyle interventions for adults with severe mental illness: A meta-review of the evidence
pmc-11733621.creator: Isabel Maurus, Sarah Wagner, Johanna Spaeth, Anastasia Vogel, Susanne Muenz, Valentina Seitz, Peter von Philipsborn, Marco Solmi, Joseph Firth, Brendon Stubbs, Davy Vancampfort, Mats Hallgren, Tamás Kurimay, Markus Gerber, Christoph U Correll, Wolfgang Gaebel, Hans-Jürgen Möller, Andrea Schmitt, Alk
pmc-11733621.description: There is growing interest in lifestyle interventions as stand-alone and add-on therapies in mental health care due to their potential benefits for both physical and mental health outcomes. We evaluated lifestyle interventions focusing on physical activity, diet, and sleep in adults with severe mental illness (SMI) and the evidence for their effectiveness.

pmc-13568610.creator: Jesús A. Acevedo Cintrón, Jonathon Blake Schofield, Daniel A. Hunter, Pranay Singh, Alexa M. Negrón Morales, Lauren Schellhardt, Susan E. Mackinnon, Matthew D. Wood

pmc-13582456.title: From benchmarking to global leadership: Singapore’s health sciences authority’s journey to WHO maturity level 4 and WHO-Listed Authority status for medicines
pmc-13582456.creator: Dorothy Toh, Adena Lim, Agnes Chan, Alvin Chia, Pei San Ang, Annie Tan, Belinda Foo, Betty Chan, Limei Chong, Qiuyi Choo, Chih Tzer Choong, Christine Ho, Siew Wei Chua, Shin Chet Chuah, Clare Louise Rodrigues, Damian Chuah, Debbie Sun, Diana Koh, Doris Yeo, Esther Tan, Eugene Goh, Evelyn Lee, Flavia
pmc-13582456.description: This article aims to describe Singapore Health Sciences Authority’s (HSA’s) multi-year journey to attaining World Health Organisation (WHO) Maturity Level 4 (ML4) and WHO-Listed Authority (WLA) status for medicines regulatory functions, presenting HSA as a descriptive policy case study on the practical application of the WHO Global Benchmarking Tool (GBT) and WLA frameworks.
